description: The paper describes a basic ordinary differential equation (ODE) model of cholera transmission, adapted from Codeço (2001), featuring Susceptible (S), Infectious (I), and Recovered (R) human compartments, plus a compartment for the bacterial concentration in a water reservoir (B). It further discusses modifications to this model to incorporate asymptomatic infections, waning immunity, and the effects of various public health interventions, including treatment, vaccination, and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) measures.
